newsitem.title: USA: Pioneer to buy OxyChem plant.
newsitem.headline: Pioneer to buy OxyChem plant.

text.p: Pioneer Cos Inc said Thursday it agreed to purchase Occidental Chemical Corp's chlor-alkali plant in Tacoma, Wash., for $102.5 million, consisting of $97 million in cash and $5.5 million of Pioneer preferred stock convertible into 440,000 common shares.
Pioneer said it has also agreed to supply a portion of the Tacoma facility's chlorine output to Occidental Petroleum Corp's OxyChem for up to five years.
The closing of the transaction, which is expected to take place by June 30, is conditioned upon obtaining financing as well as other matters, Pioneer said.

The plant has a capacity of 225,000 tons of chlorine and 247,500 tons of caustic soda. Pioneer noted it presently operates two plants with a combined capacity of 345,000 tons of chlorine and 379,500 tons of caustic soda.
It said the production of the Tacoma facility will be marketed in conjunction with the production of its Henderson, Nev., plant, which will enable the company to achieve certain economics of scale.
Pioneer now has nearly 9.2 million shares outstanding.
